Observed at +14.855287790298462s — page 7
`429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when
present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help

.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,
`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment
for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per env

ironment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentI
d}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n
| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when ther
e was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}
/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/ses
sions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-ex
ecution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rot
ate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | I
nvite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Re
move someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a d

ifferent environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.**
It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most impo
rtant thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> lea
k. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.\n>\n> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather th
an waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a
session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited\n> member get

s a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate resp

onses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass
over them. Read these in

cost order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it do
es |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` sp
lits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **C
heck `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current windo
w — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed o
nes included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, w
hich is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `2
02` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release
a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismi
ss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{fi

ndingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,
`pending`, `runnin
g`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete wo
rk;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` a

nd `projectionFailed` describe
the map independently. Reading this response never starts analysis.

Taxonomy entries carry the
published version and discovery status. Theme ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversi
on can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment com

pletes. These are
current views with version provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysi
s.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a\nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsamp
ling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the u

nmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose
.\nTheir upstream projections grow with the product and the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list would turn every

new metric into a spec
violation. Read what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes *
*no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.\n> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> in
sights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a

second slice, which is
> why it is never inferred from anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to t

he MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or oth
er feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201
{ id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-
After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictly — an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key wi
th different content is `409`). **The text goes to the MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |\n\n>

[!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.
> Include the failing call's `x-request-i
d` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it lets the team find that request in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in

the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning** — one

read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilit

ies` | The caller's role, the beta gate's state, plan limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is
a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write still enforces\n> independently, so a `true` here that races a flag flip costs you a
clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect success — and nothing should consult it\n> *instead of* trying. It exists because agent su
rfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is built with no organization in hand, so the alternative is\n> attempting the write and

reading the failure, by which point the agent has
> usually already told someone what it was about to do.

The same surface is
available as an [OpenAPI\nspecification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)\nfo

r Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When
your test users\ncan't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can

sign in itself and upload the fresh token
to a named account before each run.
